title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback operational score discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than any single submetric. Using a synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator we ran 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive artifacts (raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, analysis CSVs, and full SHA‑256 hashes). All 200 test pairs validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined on this held‑out set because labels are constant. Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the preserved bundle; we (i) map every principal claim to exact persisted artifact path(s) and SHA‑256, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe limited to preserved artifacts, and (iii) give an explicit artifact‑hygiene checklist required to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs promise intent→configuration automation for NetOps but operational authority requires defensible evidence that proposed changes are safe. Typical operational safeguards include deterministic validators, canary simulation, rollback trials, and abstention policies. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to ask: can a composite canary–rollback score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) predict emulator‑measured outages better than the best single submetric? The preregistration (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee) froze model family (gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), synthetic task bank splits (train=300,val=100,test=200), metrics, and analysis plan (train L2 on submetrics via CV on train+val, evaluate AUC on held‑out test, compare via DeLong; paired bootstrap CI for differences). Our executed, fully hashed run preserved raw outputs, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, and analysis CSVs. The principal empirical outcome is a ceiling in the held‑out test: every candidate validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200), making ROC/AUC discriminative comparison undefined on the supplied bundle. This paper therefore contributes a tightly evidence‑grounded reproducibility diagnosis, deterministic reconstruction recipe, and concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist for future discriminative studies in agentic NetOps.
sections.related_work: Recent literature emphasizes generate–verify–repair GVR pipelines and tool‑augmented agent architectures for NetOps/AIOps, and the need for verifier interposition, canary trials, and rollback testing to transform generative proposals into deployable changes. Work on verifier orchestration and cost‑aware verification policies (e.g., SEVER‑style orchestration), constraint‑driven adaptation (MeshAgent), and GVR architectures motivates our focus on composite operational metrics and their reproducible evaluation. Separate lines highlight reproducibility & provenance capture for computational experiments and the need for deterministic archival of model calls, scores, and simulator logs to permit independent recomputation; our study sits at the intersection of these threads by freezing analysis and preserving exhaustive hashed artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. Preregistered study id CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task bank: synthetic deterministic generator with fixed split (train=300,val=100,test=200). Conditions: paired baseline vs guarded with shared_initial candidate generation (the same initial candidate was reused across the two conditions for each pair). Primary estimand: difference in AUC‑ROC (composite score vs best single submetric) on held‑out test; secondary estimands: AUPRC, TNR at fixed TPR, calibration (Brier). Analysis plan (frozen): extract per‑episode submetrics, train penalized logistic regression (L2) on train+val with 5‑fold CV, fix weights, evaluate AUC on held‑out test, compare via DeLong; compute paired bootstrap CI (seed=1729,R=10000) for paired difference. Execution and artifact capture. The run executed deterministically under adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with a shared_initial generation policy. Preserved artifacts include raw model outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with full validator_trace (execution/scoring/*.json), provider‑call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest and full-per‑artifact SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Scoring/validator semantics: per episode validator_trace.validation_after contains normalized_configuration, final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and valid (boolean). The preregistration defined exact extraction rules: verifier_coverage = observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count (extracted from execution/scoring/*.json), canary_sim_pass expected from canary logs, rollback_success_prob from rollback logs, LLM_confidence from provider_calls, abstention_utility from scoring or provider logs. All preserved, hashed paths are referenced below.
sections.results: Artifact‑grounded empirical facts (from preserved artifacts). Execution manifest: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (execution/execution_manifest.json; manifest and per‑artifact hashes preserved). Held‑out test outcomes (extracted from execution/scoring/*.json): baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The persisted paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) records n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0. Inferential outputs computed from preserved analysis artifacts: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000). Status of preregistered primary estimand. Because the test labels are constant (no outages observed), ROC/AUPRC metrics are degenerate: AUC is undefined when one class is absent. Therefore the preregistered AUC‑ROC composite‑vs‑best‑submetric comparison cannot be computed from the preserved bundle. Missing preregistered persisted artifacts (artifact‑grounded). Two preregistered artifacts required to compute the primary AUC comparison are NOT present in the bundle: (1) consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode rows with verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility), and (2) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized trained L2 coefficients and normalization metadata). Per‑submetric availability (artifact‑grounded extraction mapping): - verifier_coverage: PRESENT — can be computed from execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and required_command_count (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). - canary_sim_pass: ABSENT — no canary_sim_* boolean found in execution/provider_calls/*.json or execution/scoring/*.json. - rollback_success_prob: ABSENT — no rollback trial results persisted in provider calls or scoring JSONs. - LLM_confidence: ABSENT — no numeric confidence field present in execution/provider_calls/*.json. - abstention_utility: ABSENT — no abstention fields persisted. Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑limited): using preserved artifacts one can (a) recompute per‑episode binary labels from execution/scoring/*.json → validator_trace.validation_after.valid, (b) compute verifier_coverage per episode as observed_touched_field_count/required_command_count, (c) reproduce the paired contingency table and McNemar/bootstrap CI from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (both present and hashed). However, to reconstruct missing submetrics (canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) deterministically one would need either (i) the consolidated_submetrics.csv, (ii) deterministic canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json persisted at runtime, or (iii) a replayable simulator plus preserved simulator inputs; such logs are not present in the bundle so the composite‑model pipeline cannot be recomputed without re‑execution beyond the preserved artifacts. Representative episode (artifact pointers). task-000001 baseline scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with final_state, normalized_configuration, observed_touched_field_count, required_command_count and valid=true; the shared_initial candidate is persisted at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...). These representative files concretely support the paired counts and the paired contingency table.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational implications. The deterministic validator plus shared_initial generation policy and the chosen synthetic task bank produced a ceiling effect on the held‑out partition: every generated candidate satisfied validation predicates in both conditions. Scientifically this is a valid null/ceiling outcome: discriminative metrics that require both classes (ROC/AUPRC) are undefined when one class is missing. Operational implication: discriminative evaluations of composite safety metrics require holdout partitions seeded to include adverse outcomes (e.g., injected faults, adversarial tasks, or domain shifts) so that AUC comparisons are informative. Reproducibility diagnosis and remediation. The evidence bundle contains all artifacts needed to verify the paired contingency inference and recompute the paired bootstrap/McNemar outputs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1b..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b7...). The absent consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl are deterministic artifacts that should have been persisted at runtime; their omission prevents recomputing the preregistered AUC comparison without re‑running canary/rollback simulators or regenerating missing logs. Deterministic reconstruction recipe (summary): (1) recompute binary labels from execution/scoring/*.json → validator_trace.validation_after.valid; (2) recompute verifier_coverage from validator_trace fields; (3) if canary/rollback logs are present, derive canary_sim_pass and rollback_success_prob and assemble consolidated_submetrics.csv; (4) train L2 per preregistration with the recorded RNG seed and persist composite_model_weights.pkl; (5) evaluate AUC on test. Absent steps (3)–(4) cannot be completed from the bundle alone. Artifact‑hygiene checklist (concrete filenames & canonical fields to persist at runtime). To ensure future discriminative evaluations are computable from an artifact bundle, persist at runtime: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv — columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility (CSV). 2) composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized L2 coefficients, intercept, feature normalization metadata, training RNG seed. 3) canary_simulator_log.json — per‑episode deterministic simulator outputs and SHA‑256. 4) rollback_trial_log.json — per‑episode rollback trial outputs and SHA‑256. 5) retrain_script.py and requirements.txt with pinned versions and the RNG seed used for training. These exact filenames and canonical field names are minimal and were selected to permit deterministic recomputation without re‑calling the model-serving endpoint. Threats to validity. Internal: shared_initial reduces generation variance but may mask prompt sensitivity; deterministic seeds and sensitivity checks with independent generation are recommended. Construct: emulator outages approximate production outage risk and may not capture all real‑device nondeterminism. External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks limit generality. Conclusion. The execution is artifact-complete for verifying the paired ceiling outcome but lacks two preregistered persisted artifacts needed to recompute the primary AUC comparison. We therefore (i) release the manifested hashes and representative scoring JSONs so external auditors can verify the reported paired inference, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe limited to preserved artifacts, and (iii) provide an actionable artifact capture checklist so future preregistered discriminative studies produce non‑degenerate, fully reproducible AUC comparisons without re‑execution.
sections.conclusion: A fully preregistered deterministic paired confirmatory run was executed and exhaustively hashed. Persisted artifacts show every held‑out test example validated successfully in both baseline and guarded conditions (n11=200), yielding a ceiling outcome that prevents the preregistered discriminative AUC comparison. Two preregistered deterministic artifacts (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) were not persisted and thus the composite‑vs‑single AUC comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle. We mapped each principal claim to exact artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 hashes, provided a deterministic reconstruction recipe constrained to preserved artifacts, and supply a concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames and canonical fields) required to enable future non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in agentic NetOps research.

disclosure_statement: Human role and autonomy boundary. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Persisted artifacts and key SHA‑256 references (representative subset). Execution manifest and full-per-artifact hashes: execution/execution_manifest.json (manifest includes full file list and hashes; see execution manifest in bundle). Representative artifacts that directly support principal claims: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Missing preregistered persisted artifacts (artifact-grounded). The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode submetrics) and composite_model_weights.pkl (trained composite model). Neither file is present in the preserved manifest; therefore the preregistered AUC‑ROC comparison cannot be recomputed from the bundle alone. Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). The autonomous researcher did not request, accept, or incorporate manual human revisions to the manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real‑world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
